• Mahendravarman I (Pallava Dynasty): Ruled circa 590–630 CE; laid the foundation of great Pallava power and architecture, making Event 2 the earliest among the given options.
• Gopala (Pala Dynasty): Elected king around 750 CE, ending the period of anarchy (matsyanyaya) in Bengal, placing Event 4 second.
• King Bhoja / Mihira Bhoja (Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty): Ascended the throne in circa 836 CE and ruled until 885 CE, consolidating Pratihara power and placing Event 1 third.
• Parantaka I (Imperial Cholas): Ruled from circa 907 to 955 CE, expanding Chola supremacy in the south, making Event 3 the latest.
• Chronological sequence: Mahendravarman I (c. 600 CE) → Gopala (c. 750 CE) → Bhoja (c. 836 CE) → Parantaka I (c. 907 CE), giving 2 – 4 – 1 – 3.
• Why Option A is incorrect: It places Bhoja (1) before Gopala (4), whereas the Pala dynasty was founded in 750 CE, decades before Bhoja's accession in 836 CE.
• Why Option B is incorrect: It wrongly begins with Parantaka I (3), who ruled in the 10th century CE, which is the latest event, not the earliest.
• Why Option D is incorrect: It also incorrectly begins with Parantaka I (3) and ends with Mahendravarman I (2), completely reversing the timeline.
• Often confused with: Candidates often confuse King Bhoja of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty (9th century CE) with King Bhoja of the Paramara dynasty of Malwa (11th century CE, c. 1010–1055 CE). Similarly, Parantaka I (c. 907 CE) is often confused with Vijayalaya (c. 850 CE), who initially revived Chola rule from Thanjavur.
